question.problem: Which of the following represents the streamlines of the vector field $F(x,y)=(x-1)i-y\,j$ over the domain $D={R}^{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
The streamlines of a vector field are the level curves of its stream function and are tangential to the vector field at every point. 

If $F$ represents the velocity field of a fluid flow, then they show the path traced out by a massless particle as it moves with the flow.

A vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ with a simply connected domain $D⊆{R}^{2}$ has a stream function $ψ(x,y)$ if and only if

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=0.
$$

Note that 

$$
F(x,y)=(x-1)i-y\,j
$$

 is a vector field with simply connected domain $D,$ where $P(x,y)=x-1$ and $Q(x,y)=-y.$ Computing the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=1,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $F$ has a stream function, since

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=1-1=0.
$$

Next, we find a stream function. A function $ψ(x,y)$ is a stream function of the vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ if 

$$
P=\frac{∂ψ}{∂y},\,Q=-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\frac{∂ψ}{∂y}=x-1,\,\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}=y.
$$

Integrating these equations, we obtain the following:

$$
ψ(x,y)=xy-y+f(x),\,ψ(x,y)=xy+g(y)
$$

where $f$ and $g$ are arbitrary functions. Finally, setting $f(x)=0$ or $g(y)=-y,$ we have

$$
ψ(x,y)=xy-y.
$$

Finally, we find the level curves of the stream function $ψ(x,y)=xy-y$ given by the equations $ψ(x,y)=c.$

Notice that the range of $ψ(x,y)$ is $(-\infty ,\infty ).$ So, we will consider level curves for any value of $c.$ So, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}ψ(x,y) & =c \\ xy-y & =c \\ y(x-1) & =c \\ y & =\frac{c}{x-1}\end{aligned}
$$

The equation above gives us a family of hyperbolas with asymptotes $y=0$ and $x=1$ and, for $c=0,$ the lines $y=0$ and $x=1.$ Therefore, the correct graph (along with the vector field $F$) is as follows:
